text:
Chicago is 5-13-1 with 11 points, and our playoff race has the Blackhawks at effectively zero. The chances agree it isn't bad luck: they get 42% of the expected goals and allow 4.11 goals a game.

The off-ice noise is about the bench and the front office. Connor Bedard said the players have "100 percent belief" in Jeff Blashill, per NHL.com, which tells you the question is being asked. Bowen Byram's long absence has turned into its own talking point, and the rumor mill keeps pairing Chicago with names who could help Bedard.

The goaltending broke first. Arvid Soderblom went 0-3-1 at .846 over his last four starts, then cleared waivers and went to Rockford. The defense is the deeper problem: the young pair of Wyatt Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov has been on for four goals for and 15 against, with 32% of the expected goals. That's a young defenseman learning the hardest possible way.

There was relief Thursday. Patrick Kane, back from a three-game injury absence, said "It feels good to win" after Ryan Donato won it in overtime against Buffalo. Tyler Bertuzzi has one point in 10 games on 5.3 expected, so his chances have been better than his luck. Watch Bedard's line with Kane and Roman Kantserov: it's been outshot badly, and whether it can tilt the ice is the real measure of this season.
headline: The Blackhawks' rebuild is still taking its lumps
